definition_en: a piece of work given to someone, or the act of giving it out
core_image: 一张写好的任务纸被放到桌上
scene: 课代表把一摞纸发下来。The whole class groaned at the assignment.
sceneCN: 这里 assignment 是「作业」（第 1 个义项：布置下来的任务）；句意是全班看到作业都叹气。

senses.title: Work given to someone
senses.definition: a piece of work given to a person as part of their job or study
senses.definitionCN: 作为工作或学业的一部分分派给某人的活儿
senses.example: The whole class groaned at the assignment.
senses.exampleCN: 全班看到这份作业都叹气。
senses.why: Assignment is assign plus -ment, and this suffix turns the act of allotting into the thing allotted, so it names the work that lands on a person's desk.
senses.whyCN: assignment 是 assign 加 -ment，这个后缀把「分派」的动作变成被分派的东西，所以它指落到某人桌上的那份活。

senses.title: Act of allocating
senses.definition: the act of giving out duties, rights or property
senses.definitionCN: 把职责、权利或财产分出去的行为
senses.example: The assignment of seats took ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 分配座位花了十分钟。
senses.why: The same suffix can also name the action itself, so assignment keeps an abstract sense of the handing-out process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也能指动作本身，因此 assignment 保留了「分发这一行为」的抽象义。

intro.en: Assignment is the noun built on assign, a word about marking a name on a list.
intro.cn: assignment 是由 assign 构成的名词，而 assign 本指在名册上标出名字。

items.en: signum meant 'a mark or sign'.
items.cn: signum 意为「标记、符号」。

items.en: assignare meant 'to mark out and allot'.
items.cn: assignare 意为「标出并分派」。

items.en: assigner carried the sense 'to allot or appoint'.
items.cn: assigner 表示「分派、指定」。

items.en: English assignen meant 'to allot or fix'.
items.cn: 英语 assignen 意为「分派、确定」。

items.en: The suffix -ment produced assignment, the task or the act of giving it.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 构成 assignment，指任务，也指分派这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assign family; the near-meaning group names work and duties.
note.cn: 形近组是 assign 词族；近义组是表示工作与职责的词。

entries.definition: to give out as a share
a piece of work to be done
something one is required to do

normalIntro.en: An assignment is the paper that appears on your desk after a name has been marked beside it.
normalIntro.cn: assignment 就是名字被标在旁边之后，出现在你桌上的那份东西。

normal.en: The verb is assign, the noun adds -ment.
normal.cn: 动词是 assign，名词在后面加 -ment。

normal.en: It covers both school work and tasks given at work.
normal.cn: 它既可指学校作业，也可指工作中的任务。

normal.en: On assignment means sent somewhere to do a job.
normal.cn: on assignment 指被派到某处执行任务。

normal.en: The middle syllable carries the stress: as-SIGN-ment.
normal.cn: 重音在中间音节。

normal.en: Do not drop the g in writing.
normal.cn: 书写时不要漏掉 g。

abstract.en: See a stack of papers with one name written on top.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞纸，最上面写着一个名字。

abstract.en: See a blank square on a calendar filled in by another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上的空格被别人的手填上。

abstract.en: See a desk lamp on at midnight over unfinished work.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜台灯下还没做完的活。

examples.en: The whole class groaned at the assignment.
examples.cn: 全班看到这份作业都叹气。

examples.en: The assignment of seats took ten minutes.
examples.cn: 分配座位花了十分钟。

examples.en: She finished the assignment before dinner.
examples.cn: 她在晚饭前完成了作业。

dict_mnemonic.text: assign（分派）加 -ment（名词后缀）：被分派下来的东西是任务、作业；分派这个动作本身也叫 assignment。

root: 由 assign 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；assign 源自拉丁语 assignare「标出、分派」，因此 assignment 既指被分派的任务，也指分派行为。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is the work itself, the other is the act of handing it out.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项是那份活本身，另一个义项是把活分出去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of work with a name written at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份写着名字的工作纸。

intro.en: The word belongs to the sign family, where a mark fixes who gets what.
intro.cn: 这个词属于 sign 词族，标记决定谁得到什么。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum, 'a mark', also underlies design, signal and signature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum「记号」也是 design、signal 与 signature 的来源。

items.meaning: a task or the act of allotting
to mark out for a role

definition_en: to help someone by doing part of the work, or to help make a goal
core_image: 有人站在旁边，伸手扶住摇晃的梯子
scene: 手术室里器械不断递到医生手边。A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 assist 是「协助」（第 1 个义项：在旁边帮忙）；句意是手术中一名护士协助外科医生。

senses.title: Help by sharing the work
senses.definition: to help someone, especially by doing part of their work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人，尤其替他分担一部分工作
senses.example: A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术中一名护士协助外科医生。
senses.why: Assist comes from Latin assistere, 'to stand by', so the picture is someone standing beside you and lending a hand rather than taking over.
senses.whyCN: assist 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，画面是有人站到你身边搭把手，而不是代替你去做。

senses.title: Help make a goal
senses.definition: in sport, to pass or play so that another player scores
senses.definitionCN: 在体育比赛中传球配合，使队友得分
senses.example: He assisted the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分钟助攻了制胜球。
senses.why: The same image of standing beside and enabling another's success narrows in sport to the pass that lets a teammate score.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「站在旁边促成别人成功」的形象，在球场上收窄为那一脚让队友得分的传球。

intro.en: Assist is built from Latin words for standing, and its oldest picture is standing beside someone.
intro.cn: assist 由拉丁语中表示「站」的词构成，最古老的画面是站到某人身边。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand, to place'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站立、放置」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to take one's stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站到旁边」。

items.en: assister meant 'to be present and give help'.
items.cn: assister 意为「在场并给予帮助」。

items.en: English assisten meant 'to help or support'.
items.cn: 英语 assisten 意为「帮助、支援」。

items.en: Sport added the sense of setting up a goal.
items.cn: 体育领域增出「为进球做球」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sist root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs for helping.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sist 词根；近义组是其他表示帮助的动词。

entries.definition: to stand firmly on a claim
to make things easier for someone

normalIntro.en: To assist is to stand beside, not to stand in front.
normalIntro.cn: assist 是站到旁边，而不是站到前面代替。

normal.en: It usually takes a person as object: assist the surgeon.
normal.cn: 它通常以人作宾语：协助外科医生。

normal.en: The preposition is with for a task and in for a process.
normal.cn: 接任务用 with，接过程用 in。

normal.en: The double s comes from as- plus sist.
normal.cn: 双 s 来自 as- 与 sist 的结合。

normal.en: It is more formal than help.
normal.cn: 它比 help 正式。

normal.en: In football an assist is a pass, not a goal.
normal.cn: 足球里的助攻是一次传球，不是进球。

abstract.en: See one hand steadying a ladder while another climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶稳梯子，另一人往上爬。

abstract.en: See a nurse's hand arriving before it is asked for.
abstract.cn: 想象护士的手在开口之前就递到了。

abstract.en: See a pass rolled into the path of a runner.
abstract.cn: 想象一脚球滚到队友跑动的线路上。

examples.en: A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
examples.cn: 手术中一名护士协助外科医生。

examples.en: He assisted the winning goal in the last minute.
examples.cn: 他在最后一分钟助攻了制胜球。

examples.en: Two students assisted with the survey.
examples.cn: 两名学生协助做了这项调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（在旁边）加 sist（站）：站在旁边搭把手，就是协助；球场上帮队友得分的那一脚，就是助攻。

root: 源自拉丁语 assistere「站到旁边」，由 ad-「向」与 sistere「站」构成；由「在场支援」引申为帮助，现代又衍生出体育中的助攻义。

sensesIntro.en: Standing beside someone explains both lending a hand and setting up a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 「站在旁边」既能解释搭把手，也能解释为队友做球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching in from the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：从侧面伸过来的一只手。

intro.en: Assist belongs to the sist family, where the root means standing.
intro.cn: assist 属于 sist 词族，这个词根表示「站」。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, 'to stand', also gives insist, resist and persist.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere「站」还产生了 insist、resist 与 persist。

items.meaning: to stand firm on a claim

definition_en: help given to someone, especially official or financial help
core_image: 一只手从旁边伸过来，托住快要倒下的东西
scene: 老人提着两袋菜站在楼梯口。A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
sceneCN: 这里 assistance 是「帮助」（第 1 个义项：给予的援手）；句意是邻居主动帮忙提袋子。

senses.title: Help that is given
senses.definition: help that someone gives to another person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人给予另一个人的援手
senses.example: A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居主动帮忙提袋子。
senses.why: Assistance is assist plus -ance, a suffix naming a state or an act, so it treats the help as something handed over rather than as one person's deed.
senses.whyCN: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance，这个后缀表示状态或行为，因此它把帮助看作被递过来的一份援手，而不是某个人的一次动作。

senses.title: Official or financial aid
senses.definition: money or support provided by an institution or government
senses.definitionCN: 由机构或政府提供的钱款与支援
senses.example: The family applied for government assistance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人申请了政府补助。
senses.why: When the hand that helps belongs to an office or a fund rather than a neighbour, the word settles into the sense of formal aid paid out by an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当伸出的手来自机构或基金而不是邻居时，这个词就固定指由机构发放的正式援助与补助。

intro.en: Assistance is the abstract noun of assist, made with a suffix of state and action.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 的抽象名词，由表示状态与行为的名词后缀构成。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站在旁边」。

items.en: assister meant 'to be present and help'.
items.cn: assister 意为「在场帮忙」。

items.en: English formed assistance from assist on the French pattern.
items.cn: 英语仿照法语构词法，由 assist 造出 assistance。

items.en: The word widened to official and financial aid.
items.cn: 词义扩大到官方援助与资金补助。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assist family; the near-meaning group names help and support.
note.cn: 形近组是 assist 词族；近义组是表示帮助与支援的词。

entries.definition: the act of making things easier

normalIntro.en: Assistance is the help itself, not the person giving it.
normalIntro.cn: assistance 指帮助本身，不指给帮助的人。

normal.en: It is uncountable: some assistance, not an assistance.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 some assistance，不说 an assistance。

normal.en: The fixed phrases are with the assistance of and be of assistance.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 with the assistance of 与 be of assistance。

normal.en: For the person, use assistant; for the act, use assistance.
normal.cn: 指人用 assistant，指行为用 assistance。

normal.en: It sounds more formal than help.
normal.cn: 它比 help 正式。

normal.en: Financial assistance is a common official phrase.
normal.cn: financial assistance 是常见的官方说法。

abstract.en: See a hand catching a box before it falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在箱子落地前托住它。

abstract.en: See a form signed so that money can be released.
abstract.cn: 想象一份表格签好，钱才能发放。

abstract.en: See a stranger holding a door without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象陌生人没被请求就替你扶住门。

examples.en: A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
examples.cn: 一位邻居主动帮忙提袋子。

examples.en: The family applied for government assistance.
examples.cn: 这家人申请了政府补助。

examples.en: She finished the report with the assistance of two colleagues.
examples.cn: 在两位同事的帮助下，她完成了报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: assist（协助）加 -ance（行为、状态）：被给出来的援助。邻里的援手是帮助，机构发放的钱款是补助。

root: 由 assist 加 -ance 构成；assist 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，因此 assistance 指被提供的援手，现代常指机构发放的正式援助与补助。

sensesIntro.en: A hand from a neighbour and funds from an office are both help that is handed over.
sensesIntro.cn: 邻居伸的手与机构拨的钱，都是被递过来的一份帮助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steadying hand arriving from the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：从侧面伸来的一只扶持的手。

branches.en: with the assistance of a friend

intro.en: The -ance ending marks a noun of state, as in resistance and insistence.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ance 表示状态名词，resist 与 insist 的名词也这样构成。

latinIntro.en: The base sistere, 'to stand', is Latin, and it spreads across many English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 sistere「站」来自拉丁语，衍生出许多英语动词。

definition_en: a person who helps someone more senior, or a junior rank
core_image: 站在主事者侧后方，随时接过手里的活
scene: 诊所里，年轻人先登记病人的信息。The assistant booked the next patient in.
sceneCN: 这里 assistant 是「助手」（第 1 个义项：协助他人工作的人）；句意是助手为下一位病人登记。

senses.title: Person who helps
senses.definition: a person employed to help someone with their work
senses.definitionCN: 受雇帮助某人完成工作的人
senses.example: The assistant booked the next patient in.
senses.exampleCN: 助手为下一位病人做了登记。
senses.why: The Latin ending -ant marks the doer, so assistant is literally 'the one standing beside', the person who takes part of the work off another's hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -ant 标记动作的执行者，所以 assistant 字面就是「站在旁边的那个人」，替别人分担一部分工作。

senses.title: Junior rank before a title
senses.definition: used before a job title to show a rank below it
senses.definitionCN: 放在职位名称前，表示低一级的职位
senses.example: She was promoted to assistant manager last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天她升为副经理。
senses.why: A helper who stands beside a senior post naturally gave a name to the rank just under it, so the noun came to modify titles directly.
senses.whyCN: 站在主管职位旁边的帮手，很自然成了紧挨其下的那一级职务的名称，于是这个名词直接修饰职位头衔。

intro.en: Assistant turns the verb assist into a person by way of a Latin ending for the doer.
intro.cn: assistant 借拉丁语表示「做事者」的后缀，把动词 assist 变成指人的名词。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站在旁边」。

items.en: assistens was 'the one standing by'.
items.cn: assistens 指「站在旁边的人」。

items.en: English assistant named a helper in a household or office.
items.cn: 英语 assistant 指家庭或事务所里帮忙的人。

items.en: Shop assistant and assistant manager fixed the modern uses.
items.cn: 店员与副经理这两种说法固定了现代用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the assist stem; the near-meaning group names helpers and deputies.
note.cn: 形近组共享 assist 词干；近义组是表示帮手与副职的词。

normalIntro.en: An assistant is defined by position: beside and slightly behind.
normalIntro.cn: 助手的位置很明确：在旁边，稍靠后。

normal.en: It is a countable person noun: an assistant, two assistants.
normal.cn: 它是可数的人称名词：一名助手、两名助手。

normal.en: In British shops a shop assistant serves customers.
normal.cn: 英式英语里 shop assistant 指售货员。

normal.en: As a title modifier it means deputy: assistant manager.
normal.cn: 作头衔修饰语时表示副职：副经理。

normal.en: The ending -ant marks the person, as in servant.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ant 标记执行者，如 servant。

normal.en: Stress falls on the second syllable: as-SIS-tant.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a second chair set slightly behind a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象办公桌后方稍偏处摆着第二把椅子。

abstract.en: See a clipboard passed over without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记录板被默默递过去。

abstract.en: See a nameplate that begins with the word assistant.
abstract.cn: 想象一块以「助理」开头的小名牌。

examples.en: The assistant booked the next patient in.
examples.cn: 助手为下一位病人做了登记。

examples.en: She was promoted to assistant manager last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天她升为副经理。

examples.en: A teaching assistant marked the papers.
examples.cn: 一位助教批改了试卷。

dict_mnemonic.text: assist（协助）加 -ant（做某事的人）：站在旁边帮忙的人就是助手；放在职位前，就成了副职。

root: 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，由 assist 加表示执行者的 -ant 构成；本指在场帮忙的人，后也用作职位前的「助理、副」这一级别。

sensesIntro.en: The person beside the desk and the rank just below the title come from the same position.
sensesIntro.cn: 桌旁的那个人与头衔下的一级，来自同一个「在旁边」的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second chair behind and beside the main desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：主桌后侧的第二把椅子。

intro.en: The -ant ending turns an action into the person who performs it.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ant 把动作变成执行该动作的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, 'to stand', is the base of a large family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere「站」是英语中一大族词的词基。

definition_zh: 联想；把……联系起来；交往；同事
definition_en: to connect things in the mind, to spend time with people, or a person you work with
core_image: 两条原本分开的线在脑中打了一个结
scene: 一闻到消毒水味，她就想起医院。That smell is associated with the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 associate 是「联想到」（第 1 个义项：把两件事在脑中连起来）；句意是那股气味让人联想到医院。

senses.title: Connect in the mind
senses.definition: to connect one thing with another in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中把一件事与另一件事连起来
senses.example: That smell is associated with the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让人联想到医院。
senses.why: Associate comes from Latin associare, 'to join as a companion', built on socius 'companion', so the core act is pairing two things so that one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: associate 源自拉丁语 associare「使结为同伴」，词基 socius 意为同伴，所以核心动作是把两样东西配成伴，见到一个就想起另一个。

senses.title: Spend time with people
senses.definition: to spend time with a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某群体经常相处
senses.example: He associates with artists and writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他常与画家和作家来往。
senses.why: When the companionship is between people rather than ideas, the same joining becomes the plain act of keeping company with a group.
senses.whyCN: 当「结伴」发生在人与人之间而不是概念之间时，同一个连接动作就落成了与某群人来往这一日常含义。

senses.title: Work partner
senses.definition: a person you work or do business with
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作或做生意的人
senses.example: She met a business associate at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她在机场见了一位生意伙伴。
senses.why: The noun form names the companion who has been joined to you by work, so it covers colleagues and business partners without implying friendship.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指因工作而与你结伴的人，因此既能指同事，也能指生意伙伴，并不暗示私人交情。

intro.en: Associate is built on the Latin word for a companion, and its senses all keep the idea of joining.
intro.cn: associate 建立在拉丁语「同伴」一词上，各义项都保留「结成伴」的意思。

items.en: socius meant 'companion or ally'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join with as a companion'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结为同伴」。

items.en: associer meant 'to unite or combine'.
items.cn: associer 意为「联合、结合」。

items.en: English associate covered both company and mental linking.

sensesIntro.en: Ideas, people and colleagues are all joined as companions, only the kind of partner changes.

definition_en: an organized group, or a connection between things
core_image: 一群人围着同一张桌子坐下
scene: 街角的老楼门口挂起一块新牌子。The residents formed an association to save the building.
sceneCN: 这里 association 是「协会」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的组成的团体）；句意是居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

senses.title: Organized group
senses.definition: an organized group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的组织起来的一群人
senses.example: The residents formed an association to save the building.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。
senses.why: Association is associate plus -ion, so a verb meaning 'to join as companions' becomes the body of companions who have joined, that is, an organized group.
senses.whyCN: association 是 associate 加 -ion，把「结为同伴」的动词变成结成伴的那一群人，也就是有组织的团体。

senses.title: Connection or mental link
senses.definition: a connection between two things, including one made in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的关联，也包括脑中的联想
senses.example: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。
senses.why: The same joining, once it is between facts or ideas rather than people, becomes a link that can be measured or merely felt in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「结伴」如果发生在事实或观念之间而不是人之间，就成了可以被测量或只在脑中感到的关联。

intro.en: Association is the noun of joining, used both for groups of people and for links between things.
intro.cn: association 是表示「结合」的名词，既指人的团体，也指事物之间的关联。

items.en: socius meant 'companion'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join together'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结合在一起」。

items.en: Old French associer kept the sense of uniting.
items.cn: 古法语 associer 保留「联合」之义。

items.en: Association named a guild or a body of people.
items.cn: association 指行会或一群有组织的人。

items.en: Psychology gave the word its sense of a mental link.
items.cn: 心理学赋予它「脑中联想」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the associ stem; the near-meaning group names groups and links.
note.cn: 形近组共享 associ 词干；近义组是表示团体与关联的词。

normalIntro.en: An association can be a room full of members or a thread between two facts.
normalIntro.cn: association 可以是一屋子会员，也可以是两个事实之间的一根线。

normal.en: The ending -tion marks the noun built on associate.
normal.cn: 结尾 -tion 标记由 associate 构成的名词。

normal.en: In association with means working together with another body.
normal.cn: in association with 指与另一机构合作。

normal.en: In research writing it often means a statistical link.
normal.cn: 在研究写作里它常指统计上的关联。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: as-so-ci-A-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第四个音节。

normal.en: Do not drop the second i in spelling.
normal.cn: 拼写时不要漏掉第二个 i。

abstract.en: See a long table with name cards around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，四周摆着名牌。

abstract.en: See a thin line drawn between two words on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象书页上两个词之间画了一条细线。

abstract.en: See a key ring holding many keys of one building.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼的许多钥匙串在一个环上。

examples.en: The residents formed an association to save the building.
examples.cn: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

examples.en: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。

examples.en: She works in association with a local charity.
examples.cn: 她与一家本地慈善机构合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: associate（结伴）加 -ion：结成伴的一群人是协会；结成伴的两件事是联系，脑中的联系就是联想。

root: 由 associate 加 -ion 构成；associate 源自拉丁语 socius「同伴」，因此 association 既指因共同目的结成的人群，也指事物之间乃至脑中的关联。

sensesIntro.en: People joining and ideas joining share one noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 人结成伴与观念结成伴，共用一个名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate names written on one membership list.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自的名字写在同一张会员名册上。

branches.en: an association between sleep and memory

intro.en: The -ion ending turns the verb of joining into the thing or state that results.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ion 把表示结合的动词变成结合后的事物或状态。

latinIntro.en: The root soci, 'companion', also underlies society and sociology.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 soci「同伴」也是 society 与 sociology 的来源。

definition_en: to suppose without proof, to take on a duty, or to begin to have a quality
core_image: 一件外套被人直接披到自己身上
scene: 会议没核对数据就开始讨论。Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
sceneCN: 这里 assume 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：没有证据就先当作成立）；句意是大家都假定这些数字是对的。

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe that something is true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据时先认定某事成立
senses.example: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。
senses.why: Assume comes from Latin assumere, 'to take up', so taking a claim up as your own is to accept it before it has been proved.
senses.whyCN: assume 源自拉丁语 assumere「拿起来」，把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，就是在被证实之前先接受它。

senses.title: Take on a duty
senses.definition: to take on responsibility, power or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过责任、权力或职位
senses.example: She assumed control of the company in June.
senses.exampleCN: 她在六月接管了公司。
senses.why: The literal Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives here: power or duty is picked up and carried by the new holder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的本义在这个义项里保留下来：权力或责任被新的承担者接过去扛起来。

senses.title: Begin to have a quality
senses.definition: to begin to have a particular quality or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 开始带有某种性质或外表
senses.example: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。
senses.why: Putting on an appearance is the same gesture as putting on a coat, so the word can describe a look that something takes on.
senses.whyCN: 把某种外表披到自己身上，与披上一件外套是同一个动作，因此这个词也能说某物呈现出某种样子。

intro.en: Assume is a Latin verb of taking, and every sense keeps something of that gesture.
intro.cn: assume 是拉丁语中表示「拿取」的动词，各个义项都保留着这个动作的影子。

items.en: sumere meant 'to take or take up'.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿、取」。

items.en: assumere meant 'to take to oneself'.
items.cn: assumere 意为「取到自己身上」。

items.en: assumptus was the taking up of a burden or a claim.
items.cn: assumptus 指接过负担或接受某种主张。

items.en: assumer meant 'to take on or claim'.
items.cn: assumer 意为「承担、主张」。

items.en: English added the sense of taking on an appearance.
items.cn: 英语又增出「呈现出某种外表」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sume root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of supposing and taking on.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sume 词根；近义组是表示假定与承担的动词。

to agree to do a task

normalIntro.en: Assume is always a taking: a claim, a duty or a look.
normalIntro.cn: assume 始终是一个「拿」的动作：拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表。

normal.en: The pattern assume that is common in argument.
normal.cn: 论证中常见 assume that 结构。

normal.en: Assume responsibility is the formal way to say take the blame or duty.
normal.cn: assume responsibility 是承担责任的正式说法。

normal.en: The past participle assumed can mean pretended.
normal.cn: 过去分词 assumed 可表示「假装的」。

normal.en: Do not confuse assume with presume, which is based on likelihood.
normal.cn: 不要与 presume 混淆，后者带有「有理由推定」的意味。

normal.en: The s sounds like a soft z in the middle.
normal.cn: 中间的 s 读作近似 z 的浊音。

abstract.cn: 想象一件外套被从钩子上取下，不问自穿。

abstract.en: See a signature on a line that says responsibility.
abstract.cn: 想象在写着「责任」的那一栏签下名字。

abstract.en: See a face turning the colour of the sky before rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸变成雨前天空的颜色。

examples.en: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
examples.cn: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。

examples.en: She assumed control of the company in June.
examples.cn: 她在六月接管了公司。

examples.en: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sume（拿）：把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，是假定；把权力与责任拿过来，是承担；把一副样子披上身，是呈现。

root: 源自拉丁语 assumere「取到自己身上」，由 ad-「向」与 sumere「拿」构成；由「拿过来」引申为未经证实便接受，再引申为承担职责与呈现外表。

sensesIntro.en: Taking a claim, a duty or a look are three objects of the same grasping verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表，是同一个「取」的动作面对三种对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted and placed on oneself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一样东西被拿起并放到自己身上。

intro.en: The root sume, 'to take', runs through consume, resume and presume.
intro.cn: 词根 sume 意为「拿」，贯穿 consume、resume 与 presume。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere is the base, and its compounds spread across daily English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 是词基，它的复合词遍布日常英语。

definition_en: something accepted as true without proof, or the act of taking on a duty
core_image: 一块没有验过的地基被当作稳固
scene: 报告开头先列了三条前提。The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
sceneCN: 这里 assumption 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：未经验证就被接受的前提）；句意是计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

senses.title: Thing taken as true
senses.definition: something you accept as true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 未经证明就被当作成立的前提
senses.example: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。
senses.why: Assumption is assume plus -tion, turning the act of taking a claim up into the claim itself, the thing a plan leans on before proof arrives.
senses.whyCN: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，把「拿过来接受」的动作变成被接受的那条内容，也就是计划在证据到来前所倚靠的前提。

senses.title: Act of taking on
senses.definition: the act of taking on power, duty or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过权力、职责或职位的行为
senses.example: The assumption of office takes place in May.
senses.exampleCN: 就职仪式在五月举行。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives as a formal noun for entering an office or taking up a duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的旧义保留下来，成为正式说法，指就任职位或承担职责。

intro.en: Assumption is the noun of taking up, whether a belief or an office.
intro.cn: assumption 是「拿起、接过」的名词，接过的可以是一种看法，也可以是一个职位。

items.en: Old French assumer kept both the logical and official senses.
items.cn: 古法语 assumer 兼有逻辑与职务两方面的含义。

items.en: English assumption fixed the sense of an unproved premise.
items.cn: 英语把 assumption 固定为「未经证明的前提」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sume family; the near-meaning group names premises and guesses.
note.cn: 形近组是 sume 词族；近义组是表示前提与推测的词。

a statement an argument starts from

normalIntro.en: An assumption is a floor nobody has tested before building on it.
normalIntro.cn: assumption 是一块没验过就被踩上去的地板。

normal.en: The phrase on the assumption that introduces the unproved point.
normal.cn: 短语 on the assumption that 引出那个未经验证的判断。

normal.en: In academic writing assumptions are usually stated and then tested.
normal.cn: 学术写作里通常先点明假设，再加以检验。

normal.en: The second sense is formal and appears with office or power.
normal.cn: 第二个义项较正式，常与职位或权力连用。

normal.en: The ending is -tion, so the noun refers to a thing or an act.
normal.cn: 结尾是 -tion，因此名词指事物或行为。

normal.en: Do not write an assumption of that for the everyday sense.
normal.cn: 日常「假定」义不用 an assumption of that 这种结构。

abstract.en: See a house built on a slab nobody checked.
abstract.cn: 想象房子盖在一块没人检查过的板上。

abstract.en: See a question mark drawn over a number in a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告里的数字上被画了问号。

abstract.en: See a hand receiving a seal of office.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手接过任职印章。

examples.en: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
examples.cn: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

examples.en: Her argument begins with a false assumption.

dict_mnemonic.text: assume（假定、承担）加 -tion：被拿过来当作前提的那条内容是假设；把职位接过来这件事本身，是就任。

sensesIntro.en: A belief picked up without proof and an office picked up in ceremony are both things taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 未经证明就接受的看法，与在仪式上接过的职位，都是被「拿起」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a floor laid down before anyone tests it.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人验过就铺好的地板。

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin sense of taking, with -tion marking the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留拉丁语「拿取」之义，-tion 标记结果。

latinIntro.en: Sumere, 'to take', gives a whole set of English nouns in -tion.
latinIntro.cn: sumere「拿」产生了一整组以 -tion 结尾的英语名词。

definition_en: to tell someone confidently that something is true, or to make it certain
core_image: 一只手按住对方的手背，说一句放心
scene: 登机前机长在广播里说明情况。The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 assure 是「向……保证」（第 1 个义项：让对方确信某事）；句意是机长向我们保证航班安全。

pos.zh: 动词：向……保证；使确信；确保

derivatives.zh: 形容词：确信的；有把握的

senses.title: Make someone certain
senses.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true so they stop worrying
senses.definitionCN: 肯定地告诉对方某事为真，使其不再担心
senses.example: The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
senses.exampleCN: 机长向我们保证航班是安全的。
senses.why: Assure comes from Latin assecurare, 'to make secure', built on securus 'free from care', so the core act is removing someone's worry rather than merely stating a fact.
senses.whyCN: assure 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安全」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，所以它的核心是替对方消除担心，而不只是陈述事实。

senses.title: Make certain to happen
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen or be obtained
senses.definitionCN: 使某事确定发生或确定得到
senses.example: Hard work assured his place in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 努力让他在队里站稳了位置。
senses.why: When the calming is done by events rather than words, the same 'make secure' means making an outcome certain.
senses.whyCN: 当让人安心的不是言语而是事情本身时，同一个「使稳固」就变成让某个结果确定无疑。

intro.en: Assure began as a word about making people free from care.
intro.cn: assure 起初是个让人免于忧虑的词。

items.en: securus meant 'free from care'.

items.en: English assure covered both promising and securing.
items.cn: 英语 assure 兼指保证与确保。

items.en: The word settled in formal promises and insurance.
items.cn: 这个词固定在正式承诺与保险语境中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sure family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of promising.

entries.definition: to say one will do something

normalIntro.en: To assure is to hand someone a reason to stop worrying.

normal.en: The object is a person: assure the passengers.
normal.cn: 宾语是人：向乘客保证。

normal.en: Use assure someone of something or assure someone that.
normal.cn: 用 assure someone of something 或 assure someone that。

normal.en: Rest assured is a fixed phrase meaning be sure.

normal.en: Do not confuse it with ensure, which means make certain.
normal.cn: 不要与 ensure 混淆，后者意为确保。

normal.en: The ending sounds like sure.
normal.cn: 词尾读音与 sure 相同。

abstract.en: See a hand pressed briefly over another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在另一只手背上轻按一下。

abstract.en: See a seat belt sign switched off after the words are spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象广播说完后安全带指示灯熄灭。

abstract.en: See a knot pulled tight so it cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被拉紧，不会松开。

examples.en: She assured me of her support.
examples.cn: 她向我保证会支持我。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sure（安稳）：把安稳送到对方心里，就是让对方确信；把事情办到没有疑问，就是确保。

root: 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安稳」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，经古法语 asseurer 进入英语；由「让人安心」引申为口头保证，再由「使确定」引申为确保。

sensesIntro.en: Words can calm a person, and facts can settle an outcome; both remove doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 言语能安抚人，事实能定下结果，两者都在消除疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed down to steady another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下去，让另一只手稳住。

branches.en: assure a place in the team

intro.en: The root sure, 'free from care', links assure with ensure and insure.
intro.cn: 词根 sure 意为「无忧」，把 assure 与 ensure、insure 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus, 'free from care', also gives secure and security.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus「无忧」也是 secure 与 security 的来源。

definition_en: to surprise someone very much, or to shock by something hard to believe
core_image: 一声雷在头顶炸开，人愣在原地
scene: 魔术师从帽子里变出一只活鸽子。The trick astonished the children.
sceneCN: 这里 astonish 是「使惊讶」（第 1 个义项：因意外而让人愣住）；句意是这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

pos.zh: 动词：使大为惊讶；使震惊

senses.title: Surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone very much by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料之事而让人极为惊讶
senses.example: The trick astonished the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。
senses.why: Astonish goes back to Latin extonare, 'to strike with thunder', so the original picture is a person stunned by a clap overhead.
senses.whyCN: astonish 可追溯到拉丁语 extonare「雷击」，最初的画面就是人被头顶的一声雷震得愣住。

senses.title: Shock by something hard to believe
senses.definition: to shock someone with news or an event that seems unbelievable
senses.definitionCN: 用难以相信的消息或事件使人震惊
senses.example: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。
senses.why: When the thunderbolt is bad news rather than a trick, the same stunned stillness reads as shock, which is why the word also covers disbelief at something grave.
senses.whyCN: 当那道雷不是戏法而是坏消息时，同样的僵住就成了一种震惊，所以这个词也能表示对严重事件的难以置信。

intro.en: Astonish is a thunder word: its ancestors describe being struck by lightning.
intro.cn: astonish 是个打雷的词，它的祖辈词描述被雷电击中。

items.en: tonare meant 'to thunder'.
items.cn: tonare 意为「打雷」。

items.en: extonare meant 'to strike with thunder'.
items.cn: extonare 意为「以雷击打」。

items.en: estoner meant 'to stun or amaze'.
items.cn: estoner 意为「震住、使惊愕」。

items.en: astonen meant 'to stun the mind'.
items.cn: astonen 意为「使心神震住」。

items.en: The spelling settled as astonish, with the thunder forgotten.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astonish，打雷的画面渐渐被遗忘。

note.en: The look-alike group is the astonish family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 astonish 词族；近义组是其他表示惊讶的动词。

entries.definition: to upset with a sudden event

normalIntro.en: Think of a thunderclap that leaves a person standing still.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一声雷把人劈在原地不动。

normal.en: The subject is the startling thing, the object is the person.
normal.cn: 主语是令人吃惊的事物，宾语是人。

normal.en: The adjective astonishing describes the thing, astonished the person.
normal.cn: astonishing 形容事物，astonished 形容人。

normal.en: The noun is astonishment.
normal.cn: 名词是 astonishment。

normal.en: It is stronger than surprise.
normal.cn: 它比 surprise 程度更重。

normal.en: The middle syllable is stressed: as-TON-ish.
normal.cn: 重音在中间音节。

abstract.en: See a dove pulled from an empty hat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸽子从空帽子里被拎出来。

abstract.en: See a listener frozen with a cup halfway to the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象听的人僵住，杯子停在半空。

abstract.en: See a flash and then a room gone silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光之后，整个房间静下来。

examples.en: The trick astonished the children.
examples.cn: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

examples.en: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
examples.cn: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。

examples.en: She astonished us all by finishing first.
examples.cn: 她第一个完成，让我们都很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词源里藏着「雷」：拉丁语 extonare 是被雷击中。人被雷劈中般僵住，就是大为惊讶；遇到难以相信的坏消息，就是震惊。

root: 源自拉丁语 extonare「以雷击打」，由 ex- 加强语气与 tonare「打雷」构成，经古法语 estoner 进入英语；由「被雷震住」引申为大为惊讶与震惊。

sensesIntro.en: A wonderful trick and a terrible scale of damage can both freeze a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 精彩的戏法与骇人的损失规模，都能让人僵在原地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thunderclap directly overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶炸开的一声雷。

intro.en: The word carries a hidden thunder root, ton, visible also in detonate.
intro.cn: 这个词藏着表示「雷」的词根 ton，在 detonate 里也能看到。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonare, 'to thunder', and its compounds entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其复合词经法语进入英语。

definition_en: the branch of physics that studies stars and other celestial objects
core_image: 望远镜后面的人正给一颗恒星算温度
scene: 天文台的灯彻夜亮着。She studies astrophysics at the university.
sceneCN: 这里 astrophysics 是「天体物理学」（第 1 个义项：研究天体物理性质的学科）；句意是她在大学学习天体物理学。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：天文学的；极大的

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies the physical nature of stars and other celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 用物理定律研究恒星等天体性质的分支学科
senses.example: She studies astrophysics at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习天体物理学。
senses.why: Astro- comes from Greek astron 'star' and physics from physis 'nature', so the word names the study of the nature of stars by physical laws.
senses.whyCN: astro- 来自希腊语 astron「星」，physics 来自 physis「自然」，合起来就是用物理定律研究天体本性的学问。

senses.title: The physics of a given object
senses.definition: the physical processes of a particular celestial object or system, treated as a subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 某一类天体或天体系统自身的物理过程
senses.example: The astrophysics of black holes remains a young field.
senses.exampleCN: 黑洞的物理机制研究仍是一个年轻领域。
senses.why: A discipline name can be reused for its own subject matter, so the astrophysics of black holes means the physics that governs black holes, not the whole department.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称也可以转指它研究的对象本身，所以「黑洞的天体物理」指支配黑洞的物理过程，而不是整个学科。

intro.en: Astrophysics is a modern compound of a Greek word for star and a Greek word for nature.
intro.cn: astrophysics 是近代复合词，由希腊语的「星」与「自然」两部分组成。

items.en: astron meant 'star'.
items.cn: astron 意为「星」。

items.en: physis meant 'nature'.
items.cn: physis 意为「自然」。

items.en: physica named natural science.
items.cn: physica 指自然科学。

items.en: Physics became the science of matter and energy.
items.cn: physics 成为研究物质与能量的科学。

items.en: Astrophysics was coined for the physics of celestial bodies.
items.cn: astrophysics 被造出来，专指天体的物理学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares astro or physics; the near-meaning group names neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 形近组共享 astro 或 physics；近义组是相邻学科。

entries.definition: the science of matter and energy

normalIntro.en: Astrophysics puts the laws of physics to work on stars.
normalIntro.cn: astrophysics 是把物理定律用到恒星身上。

normal.en: It is uncountable: no plural and no article.
normal.cn: 它不可数，没有复数，也不加冠词。

normal.en: Astro- marks stars, as in astronomy and astronaut.
normal.cn: astro- 表示星，如 astronomy 与 astronaut。

normal.en: The person is an astrophysicist, not an astrophysician.
normal.cn: 研究的人是 astrophysicist，不是 astrophysician。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: as-tro-PHY-sics.
normal.cn: 重音在第四音节。

normal.en: It differs from astronomy by asking how, not just where.
normal.cn: 它与天文学的区别在于追问机制，而不只是位置。

abstract.en: See a telescope pointed at one bright dot.
abstract.cn: 想象望远镜对准一个亮点。

abstract.en: See a notebook full of temperatures and masses.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满温度与质量的笔记。

abstract.en: See a star drawn on a blackboard with arrows for forces.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上画着一颗星，旁边标着力。

examples.en: She studies astrophysics at the university.
examples.cn: 她在大学学习天体物理学。

examples.en: The astrophysics of black holes remains a young field.
examples.cn: 黑洞的物理机制研究仍是一个年轻领域。

examples.en: Modern astrophysics relies on data from space telescopes.
examples.cn: 现代天体物理学依赖空间望远镜的数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: astro-（星）加 physics（物理学）：用物理定律研究恒星与星系，就是天体物理学。

root: 由希腊语 astron「星」与 physis「自然」构成的近代复合词；astro- 指天体，physics 指物理研究，合起来即用物理定律研究天体的学科。

sensesIntro.en: The name of the field can also name the physical workings of the objects it studies.
sensesIntro.cn: 学科的名字也可以指它所研究的天体自身的物理过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a star reduced to measurable numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗星被化成可测量的数字。

intro.en: Two Greek roots, star and nature, are joined by a linking vowel.
intro.cn: 两个希腊词根「星」与「自然」由一个连接元音拼在一起。

latinIntro.en: The second element comes through Latin physica, the name for natural science.
latinIntro.cn: 第二部分经拉丁语 physica 传来，那是自然科学的旧称。

items.exampleCN: 一位年轻的天体物理学家

definition_zh: 在（某处）；在（某时）；以（某种速度、程度）
definition_en: used to show a point in place or time, or a rate and level
core_image: 手指点在地图上的一个点
scene: 两个人约在车站门口见面。We met at the station gate.
sceneCN: 这里 at 是「在」（第 1 个义项：指一个具体的点）；句意是我们在车站门口见面。

senses.title: A point in place
senses.definition: used to show an exact point or place
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个确切的地点或位置点
senses.example: We met at the station gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站门口见面。
senses.why: At goes back to Old English æt, a word for touching a point, which is why it marks a spot rather than the inside of a place.
senses.whyCN: at 可追溯到古英语 æt，本指触到某一点，所以它标的是一个位置点，而不是某地的内部。

senses.title: A point in time
senses.definition: used to show an exact moment
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个确切的时刻
senses.example: The train leaves at six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车六点开。
senses.why: The same pointing gesture moves onto the time line: a clock reading is treated as one dot on the day.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「点一下」的动作移到时间轴上：一个钟点被看成一天里的一个点。

senses.title: A rate or level
senses.definition: used to show a speed, price, level or manner
senses.definitionCN: 表示速度、价格、程度或方式
senses.example: He drove at sixty miles an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他以每小时六十英里的速度开车。
senses.why: Fixing a value at one point on a scale is the same act of pointing, so the word also marks rates, prices and states.
senses.whyCN: 把数值定在刻度上的某一点，也是同一个「指」的动作，因此这个词也用来标速度、价格与状态。

intro.en: At is one of the oldest English prepositions, and its meaning has stayed close to 'touching a point'.
intro.cn: at 是英语最古老的介词之一，含义一直贴近「触到一点」。

items.en: æt meant 'at, near, in'.
items.cn: æt 意为「在、靠近、于」。

items.en: Cognates in related languages also meant 'at'.
items.cn: 同语系语言中的同源词也表示「在」。

items.en: At spread to time expressions such as at night.
items.cn: at 扩展到 at night 这类时间说法。

items.en: Fixed phrases with rates and prices became common.
items.cn: 表示速度与价格的固定说法开始常见。

items.en: At remains a core preposition of point and level.
items.cn: at 至今仍是表示「点」与「刻度」的核心介词。

note.en: The look-alike group is short words easily confused with at; the near-meaning group is the other place prepositions.
note.cn: 形近组是容易与 at 混淆的短词；近义组是其他地点介词。

normalIntro.en: At marks a dot, not a box: a point on a map, a clock or a scale.
normalIntro.cn: at 标的是一个点，不是一个盒子：地图上的点、钟点或刻度上的点。

normal.en: Use at for a point, in for an enclosed space, on for a surface.
normal.cn: 点用 at，封闭空间用 in，表面用 on。

normal.en: Clock times take at: at six, at noon.
normal.cn: 钟点前用 at：六点、正午。

normal.en: Rates and prices take at: at speed, at ten dollars.
normal.cn: 速度与价格前用 at。

normal.en: The weak form sounds like a short unstressed syllable.
normal.cn: 弱读时是一个很轻的短音。

normal.en: Do not use at with a period such as in the morning.
normal.cn: 表示上午这类时段时不用 at，而用 in。

abstract.en: See a fingertip pressed on one spot of a map.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在地图的某一个点上。

abstract.en: See a clock hand stopped at one number.
abstract.cn: 想象指针停在一个数字上。

abstract.en: See a needle resting on one mark of a dial.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表指针停在一个刻度上。

examples.en: We met at the station gate.
examples.cn: 我们在车站门口见面。

examples.en: The train leaves at six.
examples.cn: 火车六点开。

examples.en: He drove at sixty miles an hour.
examples.cn: 他以每小时六十英里的速度开车。

dict_mnemonic.text: at 的核心是「一点」：地点是一点，时刻是一点，速度与价格也是刻度上的一点。

root: 古英语 æt 表示「在、靠近」，本义是触到某一点；由空间上的点扩展到时间上的时刻，再扩展到速度、价格与程度等刻度。

sensesIntro.en: Place, time and rate are all treated as single points.
sensesIntro.cn: 地点、时间与速度，都被当作一个一个的点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger touching one dot.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指触到一个点。

intro.en: At is a whole word rather than a built form, but it feeds many fixed phrases and compounds.
intro.cn: at 是独立的词而非拼合词，但它养出许多固定短语与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad, 'to', is a distant cousin and appears in dozens of English prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad「向」是远亲，出现在大量英语前缀中。

definition_en: a person who competes in sport, or a person with a strong trained body
core_image: 跑道起点，一个人压着起跑线
scene: 天还没亮，跑道上已有人在练起跑。The athlete trained for months before the race.
sceneCN: 这里 athlete 是「运动员」（第 1 个义项：参加竞技体育的人）；句意是这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。

pos.zh: 名词：运动员；体格强健的人

derivatives.zh: 形容词：运动的；体格健壮的

senses.title: Competitor in sport
senses.definition: a person who competes in a sport, especially one who trains hard
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育比赛、尤其经过刻苦训练的人
senses.example: The athlete trained for months before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。
senses.why: Athlete comes from Greek athletes, 'one who competes for a prize', built on athlon 'contest or prize', so the word names a contender rather than anyone who exercises.
senses.whyCN: athlete 来自希腊语 athletes「为奖品而竞争的人」，词根 athlon 意为竞赛或奖品，所以它指参赛的竞争者，而不是任何锻炼的人。

senses.title: Strong trained body
senses.definition: a person with a strong, fit and well-trained body
senses.definitionCN: 身材健壮、训练有素的人
senses.example: Her brother is a natural athlete.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟天生体格强健。
senses.why: Since contenders are visibly fit, the word stretched from the competitor to anyone built and trained like one.
senses.whyCN: 参赛者通常体格出众，于是这个词从「参赛的人」扩展到「像运动员那样健壮的人」。

intro.en: Athlete is a Greek word for a contender, and its root names the prize itself.
intro.cn: athlete 是希腊语中表示竞争者的人，词根指的正是奖品。

items.en: athlon meant 'prize or contest'.
items.cn: athlon 意为「奖品、竞赛」。

items.en: athletes meant 'one who contends for a prize'.
items.cn: athletes 意为「为奖品而竞争的人」。

items.en: athleta kept the sporting sense.
items.cn: athleta 保留体育竞技之义。

items.en: English athlete named a competitor in games.
items.cn: 英语 athlete 指竞技比赛中的选手。

items.en: The word also came to describe a fit, trained body.
items.cn: 这个词也用来形容健壮、训练有素的身体。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the athlet stem; the near-meaning group names sports people.
note.cn: 形近组共享 athlet 词干；近义组是表示体育人士的词。

entries.definition: one who runs in a race

normalIntro.en: An athlete is someone who trains for a prize, not just someone who moves.
normalIntro.cn: athlete 是为奖品而训练的人，不只是活动身体的人。

normal.en: The th is pronounced as a plain t sound in many accents.
normal.cn: 在许多口音里 th 读作普通的 t 音。

normal.en: The adjective is athletic, the field is athletics.
normal.cn: 形容词是 athletic，田径运动是 athletics。

normal.en: It is countable: an athlete, two athletes.
normal.cn: 它可数：一名运动员、两名运动员。

normal.en: Not every fit person is an athlete in the strict sense.
normal.cn: 严格说来，体格好的人不一定都是运动员。

normal.en: The final -e is silent.
normal.cn: 词尾的 e 不发音。

abstract.en: See a foot pressed against a starting block.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抵住起跑器。

abstract.en: See a medal held up above a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象人群上方举起一枚奖牌。

abstract.en: See a body hardened by years of morning runs.
abstract.cn: 想象常年晨跑练出的身体。

examples.en: The athlete trained for months before the race.
examples.cn: 这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。

examples.en: Her brother is a natural athlete.
examples.cn: 她弟弟天生体格强健。

examples.en: Every athlete on the team passed the fitness test.
examples.cn: 队里每名运动员都通过了体能测试。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根 athlon 是「奖品、竞赛」：为奖品而竞争的人是运动员；长期训练出来的健壮体格，也被称作 athlete。

root: 源自希腊语 athlon「奖品、竞赛」与 athletes「为奖品而竞争的人」，经拉丁语 athleta 进入英语；本指参赛选手，后也形容体格健壮的人。

sensesIntro.en: The contender and the trained body are two sides of the same sporting life.
sensesIntro.cn: 参赛者与训练出来的身体，是同一种运动生涯的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body set at the start line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体伏在起跑线上。

intro.en: The athl root, 'contest', also appears in the names of multi-event sports.
intro.cn: 词根 athl 意为竞赛，也出现在多项赛事的名称里。

latinIntro.en: Greek athlon passed through Latin athleta into English and into athletic vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 athlon 经拉丁语 athleta 进入英语，形成一整套体育词汇。

items.meaning: one who contends for a prize

definition_en: the gases around the earth, or the feeling of a place or situation
core_image: 一层薄薄的空气裹着地球
scene: 房间里的笑声忽然停了。The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
sceneCN: 这里 atmosphere 是「气氛」（第 2 个义项：一个场合给人的整体感觉）；句意是屋里的气氛冷了下来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大气的；有氛围的
名词：大气干扰；气氛渲染

senses.title: Layer of gases
senses.definition: the mass of gases that surrounds the earth or another planet
senses.definitionCN: 包围地球或其他行星的气体层
senses.example: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳把热量困在大气层里。
senses.why: Atmosphere joins Greek atmos 'vapour' with sphaira 'sphere', so it literally names the ball of vapour wrapped around a planet.
senses.whyCN: atmosphere 把希腊语 atmos「气、蒸气」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，字面就是包在行星外面的一层气球。

senses.title: Feeling of a place
senses.definition: the overall feeling that a place or situation gives people
senses.definitionCN: 一个场合或情境给人的整体感受
senses.example: The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里的气氛冷了下来。
senses.why: The air that surrounds and fills a room also surrounds a group of people, so the word shifts from the physical gas to the invisible mood that fills a space.
senses.whyCN: 充满房间、包围人的空气，同样包围着一群人；于是这个词从看得见的气体转成充满空间、看不见的情绪。

intro.en: Atmosphere was coined by joining two Greek words for vapour and sphere.
intro.cn: atmosphere 是把两个希腊词「气」与「球」拼起来造出的词。

items.en: atmos meant 'vapour or steam'.
items.cn: atmos 意为「气、蒸气」。

items.en: sphaira meant 'sphere or ball'.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球体」。

items.en: Scientists coined atmosphere for the vapour around a planet.
items.cn: 科学家造出 atmosphere 一词，指包围行星的气层。

items.en: The word began to describe the mood of a place.
items.cn: 这个词开始用来描述一个场合的气氛。

items.en: Both the climate sense and the mood sense are standard.
items.cn: 大气义与气氛义都已成为标准用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sphere part; the near-meaning group names air and mood.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sphere 部分；近义组是表示空气与情绪的词。

normalIntro.en: The same word covers the air around a planet and the air of a room.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个词既指行星周围的气层，也指一屋子里的空气。

normal.en: The ph in atmosphere sounds like f.
normal.cn: atmosphere 里的 ph 读作 f。

normal.en: For the gas layer, use the definite article: the atmosphere.
normal.cn: 指大气层时常加定冠词。

normal.en: For mood, use an article: a relaxed atmosphere.
normal.cn: 指气氛时用不定冠词：轻松的气氛。

normal.en: The adjective atmospheric also means full of mood.
normal.cn: 形容词 atmospheric 也可表示「很有氛围的」。

normal.en: The sphere part is the same as in hemisphere.
normal.cn: sphere 这一部分与 hemisphere 相同。

abstract.en: See a thin glowing skin around a blue ball.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色球体外面一层发光的薄皮。

abstract.en: See a room where nobody speaks after a door shuts.
abstract.cn: 想象门关上后没人说话的屋子。

abstract.en: See breath visible in cold morning air.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷清晨里可见的呼气。

examples.en: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
examples.cn: 二氧化碳把热量困在大气层里。

examples.en: The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
examples.cn: 屋里的气氛冷了下来。

examples.en: The café has a relaxed atmosphere.
examples.cn: 这家咖啡馆气氛轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmos（气）加 sphere（球）：包着星球的一层气，是大气层；充满房间、包围人的那层感觉，是气氛。

root: 由希腊语 atmos「气、蒸气」与 sphaira「球」构成，字面指包着星球的气层；由包围人的空气引申为场所给人的整体感受。

sensesIntro.en: Something invisible fills and surrounds, whether it is gas or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 看不见的东西充满并包围四周，它可以是气体，也可以是情绪。

core.cn: 核心意象：球体外一层薄薄的气。

intro.en: The second half is the sphere family, and the first half is a Greek word for vapour.
intro.cn: 后半是 sphere 词族，前半是希腊语中表示「气」的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek sphaira reached English through Latin sphaera.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 sphaira 经拉丁语 sphaera 进入英语。

definition_en: the smallest unit of a chemical element, or a very small amount
core_image: 一颗小到不能再切开的小球
scene: 黑板上画着电子绕着中心转的圈。The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
sceneCN: 这里 atom 是「原子」（第 1 个义项：构成元素的基本微粒）；句意是原子中心有一个原子核。

derivatives.zh: 动词：使雾化；使分裂成微粒

senses.title: Smallest unit of an element
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a chemical element that can take part in a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 能参与化学反应的最小元素单位
senses.example: The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 原子中心有一个原子核。
senses.why: Atom comes from Greek atomos, 'uncut', from a- 'not' plus temnein 'to cut', because the ancients thought it could not be divided further.
senses.whyCN: atom 来自希腊语 atomos「不可切分的」，由 a-「不」与 temnein「切」构成，因为古人以为它小到不能再分。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a very small amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点分量
senses.example: There is not an atom of truth in the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传言里没有一点真实成分。
senses.why: The smallest unit of matter became a measure of the smallest possible amount, used for emphasis in negatives.
senses.whyCN: 物质的最小单位被借来度量最小可能的分量，多用于否定句以加强语气。

intro.en: Atom is a Greek word that literally says 'not cuttable'.
intro.cn: atom 是个希腊词，字面意思就是「不可切分」。

items.en: temnein meant 'to cut'.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」。

items.en: atomos meant 'indivisible'.
items.cn: atomos 意为「不可分割的」。

items.en: atomus named the smallest particle.
items.cn: atomus 指最小的微粒。

items.en: Atom entered scientific English as the basic particle.
items.cn: atom 作为基本微粒进入科学英语。

items.en: The word also became a figure for a tiny amount.
items.cn: 这个词也成了「极小分量」的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the atom family; the near-meaning group names particles and specks.
note.cn: 形近组是 atom 词族；近义组是表示微粒与少许的词。

normalIntro.en: Atom means uncut: the piece nobody could divide any further.
normalIntro.cn: atom 意为不可切分，指那块谁也无法再分的微粒。

normal.en: The word is countable: an atom, two atoms.
normal.cn: 它可数：一个原子、两个原子。

normal.en: For emphasis in negatives, use not an atom of.
normal.cn: 否定句里用 not an atom of 加强语气。

normal.en: The adjective is atomic, not atomical.
normal.cn: 形容词是 atomic，不是 atomical。

normal.en: Do not confuse atom with molecule, which is a group.
normal.cn: 不要与 molecule 混淆，后者是原子的组合。

normal.en: Stress falls on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a ball so small that no knife can enter it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小到刀锋都进不去的球。

abstract.en: See a single dot of dust on glass.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃上的一粒尘点。

abstract.en: See a diagram of rings around one centre.
abstract.cn: 想象中心周围画着几个圈的示意图。

examples.en: The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
examples.cn: 原子中心有一个原子核。

examples.en: There is not an atom of truth in the rumour.
examples.cn: 这个传言里没有一点真实成分。

examples.en: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
examples.cn: 一个水分子含两个氢原子和一个氧原子。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（不）加 tom（切）：不可再切的最小微粒，就是原子；再抽象一步，就是「一点点」。

root: 源自希腊语 atomos「不可分割的」，由 a-「不」与 temnein「切」构成，经拉丁语 atomus 进入英语；由最小微粒引申为极小的分量。

sensesIntro.en: The smallest piece of matter and the smallest possible amount share one limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 物质的最小一块与分量的最小一点，共用同一条底线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot no knife can divide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个刀也切不开的点。

intro.en: The Greek root tom, 'cut', links atom with anatomy and dichotomy.
intro.cn: 希腊词根 tom 意为「切」，把 atom 与 anatomy、dichotomy 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek atomos reached English through Latin atomus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 atomos 经拉丁语 atomus 进入英语。

definition_en: relating to atoms, or using the energy released from them
core_image: 墙上钉着一张电子绕核的模型图
scene: 实验室门口贴着辐射警示标志。The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
sceneCN: 这里 atomic 是「原子的」（第 1 个义项：与原子有关的）；句意是实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。

pos.zh: 形容词：原子的；原子能的

senses.title: Relating to atoms
senses.definition: relating to atoms or their structure
senses.definitionCN: 与原子本身或其结构有关
senses.example: The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。
senses.why: Atomic is atom plus -ic, a suffix meaning 'relating to', so it describes whatever belongs to the study or structure of atoms.
senses.whyCN: atomic 是 atom 加 -ic，这个后缀表示「与……有关」，所以它形容一切属于原子研究或原子结构的事物。

senses.title: Using nuclear energy
senses.definition: using the energy released when atomic nuclei are split or joined
senses.definitionCN: 利用原子核裂变或聚变释放的能量
senses.example: Atomic power plants supply electricity to the region.
senses.exampleCN: 核电站为这一地区供电。
senses.why: Because the first large-scale use of this energy was described as atomic, the adjective widened from the particle to the power released from it.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种能量最早被大规模使用时称作原子能，形容词就从「原子本身」扩大到「原子释放出的动力」。

intro.en: Atomic is a scientific adjective built on the Greek word for an uncut particle.
intro.cn: atomic 是建立在希腊语「不可切分的微粒」之上的科学形容词。

items.en: atomos meant 'indivisible'.
items.cn: atomos 意为「不可分割的」。

items.en: atomus named the smallest particle.
items.cn: atomus 指最小微粒。

items.en: Atom entered English as the basic unit of matter.
items.cn: atom 作为物质基本单位进入英语。

items.en: Atomic was formed to mean 'of atoms'.
items.cn: atomic 被构成，意为「原子的」。

items.en: Atomic extended to nuclear energy and weapons.
items.cn: atomic 扩展到核能与核武器领域。

note.en: The look-alike group is the atom family; the near-meaning group gives scientific adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组是 atom 词族；近义组是其他科学形容词。

normalIntro.en: Atomic describes the particle first and the power it releases second.
normalIntro.cn: atomic 先说微粒本身，再说由它释放的动力。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-TOM-ic.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: The noun is atom, the adjective adds -ic.
normal.cn: 名词是 atom，形容词加 -ic。

normal.en: For energy, atomic and nuclear are close in meaning.
normal.cn: 指能源时，atomic 与 nuclear 含义接近。

normal.en: Atomic number names the count of protons.
normal.cn: atomic number 指质子数。

normal.en: Do not write atomical in modern English.
normal.cn: 现代英语不写 atomical。

abstract.cn: 想象门上贴着三叶形的警示标志。

abstract.en: See a single lamp lit by a distant plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯由远处电厂点亮。

examples.en: The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
examples.cn: 实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。

examples.en: Atomic power plants supply electricity to the region.
examples.cn: 核电站为这一地区供电。

examples.en: The atomic number of carbon is six.
examples.cn: 碳的原子序数是六。

sensesIntro.en: The particle and the power inside it are described by one adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 微粒本身与它内部的能量，共用一个形容词。

intro.cn: 这个形容词用 -ic 结尾，与 basic、organic 相同。

latinIntro.en: Atom itself came from Greek through Latin, and the -ic ending is Latin too.

definition_zh: 系上；附上；认为有（重要性）
definition_en: to fasten one thing to another, or to connect value or feeling to it
core_image: 用别针把两张纸别在一起
scene: 填表时她随手把照片别在右上角。She attached a photo to the form.
sceneCN: 这里 attach 是「附上」（第 1 个义项：把东西固定到另一件东西上）；句意是她把照片附在表格上。

senses.title: Fasten one thing to another
senses.definition: to fasten or join one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一件东西固定或连接到另一件上
senses.example: She attached a photo to the form.
senses.exampleCN: 她把照片附在表格上。
senses.why: Attach comes from Old French atachier, 'to fasten with a nail', so the original act is pinning one object onto another.
senses.whyCN: attach 来自古法语 atachier「用钉子固定」，最初的动作就是把一件东西钉到另一件上。

senses.title: Treat as important
senses.definition: to connect value or importance to something
senses.definitionCN: 把价值或重要性系在某事上
senses.example: The school attaches great importance to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校非常重视阅读。
senses.why: Pinning a value onto a thing is a short step from pinning a label on it, so the physical fastening becomes a judgement of worth.
senses.whyCN: 把价值钉在某物上，与把标签钉在实物上只差一步，于是具体的固定动作变成了对价值的判断。

senses.title: Be emotionally tied
senses.definition: to feel affection that ties you to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 因感情而与某人某物系在一起
senses.example: She is deeply attached to her old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那辆旧自行车很有感情。
senses.why: Affection works like a rope: being attached means the tie is felt rather than seen, ending in the passive form used for fondness.
senses.whyCN: 感情像一根绳：be attached 表示这根绳看不见却能感到，于是被动形式专门用来表示依恋。

intro.en: Attach began as a word about nailing things down and grew senses of value and affection.
intro.cn: attach 起初指用钉子固定，后来长出价值与感情方面的含义。

items.en: tache meant 'a nail or fastening'.
items.cn: tache 意为「钉子、扣件」。

items.en: atachier meant 'to fasten or pin'.
items.cn: atachier 意为「固定、别住」。

items.en: attachen first meant 'to seize legally'.
items.cn: attachen 最初还有「依法扣押」之义。

items.en: The word settled on fastening things together.
items.cn: 词义固定为把东西连接在一起。

items.en: Attach importance to and be attached to developed as fixed uses.
items.cn: 重视与依恋两种说法逐渐固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attach family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of joining.
note.cn: 形近组是 attach 词族；近义组是表示连接的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attach pins one thing to another, and can pin value or feeling too.
normalIntro.cn: attach 把一件东西别到另一件上，也能把价值或感情别上去。

normal.en: The pattern is attach something to something.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 attach something to something。

normal.en: Attach importance to is a formal way to say value.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视」的正式说法。

normal.en: Be attached to usually means feel fond of.
normal.cn: be attached to 通常表示依恋。

normal.en: The double t comes from the prefix and stem meeting.
normal.cn: 双 t 来自前缀与词干相接。

normal.en: The word ends with a ch sound.
normal.cn: 词尾读作 ch 音。

abstract.cn: 想象一个回形针把两页纸别住。

abstract.en: See a price tag tied to a handle.
abstract.cn: 想象价签系在把手上。

abstract.en: See an invisible cord from a hand to an old object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手与旧物之间有一根看不见的线。

examples.en: She attached a photo to the form.
examples.cn: 她把照片附在表格上。

examples.en: The school attaches great importance to reading.
examples.cn: 这所学校非常重视阅读。

examples.en: She is deeply attached to her old bike.
examples.cn: 她对那辆旧自行车很有感情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 古法语 atachier 是「钉住」：把东西钉在一起是附上；把价值钉在某事上是重视；把感情钉在某人身上是依恋。

root: 源自 Old French atachier「用钉子固定」，词根 tache 意为钉子；由具体的「别住、连上」引申为赋予价值，再引申为情感上的依恋。

sensesIntro.en: A pin, a value and an affection are all things tied to something else.
sensesIntro.cn: 别针、价值与感情，都是系在别的东西上的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin pushed through two sheets.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根别针穿过两页纸。

branches.en: attach no weight to a claim

intro.en: The prefix a- here comes from Latin ad-, and detach reverses the act.
intro.cn: 这里的前缀 a- 来自拉丁语 ad-，而 detach 表示相反的动作。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to a Germanic word for a nail, borrowed into French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干可追溯到日耳曼语中表示钉子的词，后被法语借用。

definition_en: to use force against someone, to criticize strongly, or a sudden onset of illness
core_image: 一只手突然伸向对方
scene: 报纸头版猛烈批评了这项决定。The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
sceneCN: 这里 attack 是「抨击」（第 2 个义项：用言语猛烈批评）；句意是报纸在头版抨击这项决定。

senses.title: Use force against
senses.definition: to try to hurt or defeat someone with force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力伤害或击败对方
senses.example: The soldiers attacked the bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时进攻那座桥。
senses.why: Attack comes from Italian attaccare, 'to join battle', from a word meaning to fasten, so the core picture is closing with an enemy and engaging.
senses.whyCN: attack 来自意大利语 attaccare「接上打斗」，其词根意为「接合」，所以核心画面是贴近敌人、交上手。

senses.title: Criticize strongly
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very strongly in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或文字中猛烈批评某人某事
senses.example: The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸在头版抨击这项决定。
senses.why: A verbal assault borrows the whole martial image: words are aimed and driven at a target as if they were blows.
senses.whyCN: 言语上的攻击借用了整套交战画面：话像拳头一样被瞄准并砸向目标。

senses.title: Sudden onset of illness
senses.definition: a sudden and severe start of an illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病突然而猛烈地开始
senses.example: He had a heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年冬天心脏病发作。
senses.why: Illness arrives like an enemy raid, so its sudden onset is named with the same word as a military strike.
senses.whyCN: 疾病像敌军突袭一样到来，所以它突然开始的那一刻，就用与军事打击相同的词来命名。

intro.en: Attack entered English from Italian fighting speech and spread from battle to words and illness.
intro.cn: attack 从意大利语的交战用语进入英语，又从战场扩展到言语与疾病。

items.en: attaccare meant 'to join battle'.
items.cn: attaccare 意为「接战、交上手」。

items.en: The phrase meant 'to begin a fight'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「开始战斗」。

items.en: attaquer carried the military sense into French.
items.cn: attaquer 把军事含义带入法语。

items.en: English attack covered armed assault.
items.cn: 英语 attack 指武装攻击。

items.en: The word extended to criticism and to illness.
items.cn: 词义扩展到批评与疾病发作。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attack family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of striking and criticizing.
note.cn: 形近组是 attack 词族；近义组是表示打击与批评的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attack began as joining battle, and its force carries into words and illness.
normalIntro.cn: attack 起初是「交上手」，这股力道也带进了言语与疾病。

normal.en: It works as both verb and noun: to attack, an attack.
normal.cn: 它既是动词也是名词。

normal.en: Medical use always has an article or a modifier: a heart attack.
normal.cn: 医学用法通常带冠词或修饰语：心脏病发作。

normal.en: Under attack means being criticized or struck.
normal.cn: under attack 表示受到攻击或批评。

normal.en: The double t belongs to the stem: at-tack.
normal.cn: 双 t 属于词干。

normal.en: Attack the problem means tackle it eagerly.
normal.cn: attack the problem 指积极着手解决。

abstract.en: See a hand shooting out toward another.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手猛地伸向对方。

abstract.en: See a front page with a headline like a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象头版标题像一记拳头。

abstract.en: See a chest clutched in a crowded street.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤街道上有人捂住胸口。

examples.en: The soldiers attacked the bridge at dawn.
examples.cn: 士兵们在黎明时进攻那座桥。

examples.en: The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
examples.cn: 报纸在头版抨击这项决定。

examples.en: He had a heart attack last winter.
examples.cn: 他去年冬天心脏病发作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 意大利语 attaccare 是「接战」：贴近对手动手是攻击；把话当拳头砸过去是抨击；疾病突然扑上来是发作。

root: 源自意大利语 attaccare「接战」，与表示「接合」的词根有关，经法语 attaquer 进入英语；由武力进攻引申为言语抨击，再引申为疾病突发。

sensesIntro.en: An enemy, a critic and an illness all arrive suddenly and with force.
sensesIntro.cn: 敌人、批评者与疾病，都是突然而猛烈地扑上来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand launched at a target.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手朝目标猛伸过去。

intro.en: The word shares its shape with attach, though their senses split long ago.
intro.cn: 这个词与 attach 外形相近，不过词义早已分开。

latinIntro.en: The Italian stem is Germanic in origin, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个意大利语词干源自日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

definition_en: to reach a goal or level after effort, or to gain something
core_image: 手终于够到高处的横杆
scene: 她练了三年才拿到那张证书。After years of study she attained her goal.
sceneCN: 这里 attain 是「达到」（第 1 个义项：经过努力抵达目标）；句意是多年学习后她达到了目标。

senses.title: Reach a goal
senses.definition: to reach a goal, level or age after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力抵达某个目标、水平或年龄
senses.example: After years of study she attained her goal.
senses.exampleCN: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。
senses.why: Attain comes from Latin attingere, 'to touch', from ad- 'to' and tangere 'to touch', so success is pictured as a hand finally reaching the bar.
senses.whyCN: attain 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，成功被画成一只手终于够到横杆。

senses.title: Gain or acquire
senses.definition: to gain something such as a reputation or a position
senses.definitionCN: 取得名声、地位等抽象之物
senses.example: He attained a reputation for honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 他获得了诚实的名声。
senses.why: What a hand can touch includes not only a height but also honour and rank, so the reaching verb comes to mean acquiring.
senses.whyCN: 手能够到的不只是高度，还有荣誉与地位，于是这个「够到」的动词就有了「获得」的含义。

intro.en: Attain is a Latin word of touching, and achievement is pictured as reaching something.
intro.cn: attain 是拉丁语中表示「触碰」的词，成就被画成够到某物。

items.en: tangere meant 'to touch'.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触碰」。

items.en: attingere meant 'to touch or reach'.
items.cn: attingere 意为「触到、够到」。

items.en: ateindre meant 'to reach a goal'.
items.cn: ateindre 意为「抵达目标」。

items.en: English attain covered reaching and gaining.
items.cn: 英语 attain 兼指达到与获得。

items.en: The word now sounds formal and is common in writing.
items.cn: 这个词如今偏正式，常见于书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tain stem; the near-meaning group gives verbs of reaching and winning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tain 词干；近义组是表示抵达与取得的动词。

normalIntro.en: To attain is to get your hand on the bar at last.
normalIntro.cn: attain 就是手终于搭上那根横杆。

normal.en: It is formal; in speech people usually say reach or achieve.
normal.cn: 它偏正式，口语里更常说 reach 或 achieve。

normal.en: The object is often abstract: a goal, a level, a standard.
normal.cn: 宾语常是抽象名词：目标、水平、标准。

normal.en: The noun is attainment, not attain.
normal.cn: 名词是 attainment。

normal.en: The tain part also appears in contain and retain.
normal.cn: tain 这一部分也出现在 contain 与 retain 中。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TAIN.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See fingers closing around a high bar.
abstract.cn: 想象手指终于扣住高处横杆。

abstract.en: See a certificate handed over after long practice.
abstract.cn: 想象长期练习后递来的一纸证书。

abstract.en: See a line on a chart finally touched.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的那条线终于被碰到。

examples.en: After years of study she attained her goal.
examples.cn: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。

examples.en: He attained a reputation for honesty.
examples.cn: 他获得了诚实的名声。

examples.en: The team attained the highest standard in the test.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在测试中达到了最高标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tain（触）：手向高处伸去，终于触到，就是达到；够到名声与地位，就是获得。

root: 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，经古法语 ateindre 进入英语；由「够到」具体高度引申为达到目标与获得名声。

sensesIntro.en: Height and honour are both things a reaching hand can close on.
sensesIntro.cn: 高度与荣誉，都是伸出的手能够握住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers touching the bar.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖碰到横杆。

intro.en: The tain root, 'to hold or touch', also shapes contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: 词根 tain 意为「握住、触及」，也构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere, 'to touch', is the source; its participle tactus gives tact and contact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere「触」是来源，其分词 tactus 产生了 tact 与 contact。

definition_en: to try to do something difficult, or an act of trying
core_image: 伸手去够，指尖还差一点
scene: 他试着推开那扇卡住的门。He attempted to open the stuck door.
sceneCN: 这里 attempt 是「试图」（第 1 个义项：努力去做某事）；句意是他试图推开那扇卡住的门。

senses.title: Try to do something
senses.definition: to try to do something, especially something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 努力去做某事，尤其是困难的事
senses.example: He attempted to open the stuck door.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图推开那扇卡住的门。
senses.why: Attempt comes from Latin attemptare, from ad- 'to' and temptare 'to try or test', so it keeps the sense of reaching out to test whether a thing can be done.
senses.whyCN: attempt 源自拉丁语 attemptare，由 ad-「向」与 temptare「试、探」构成，保留着伸手试探某件事能否办成的意味。

senses.title: An act of trying
senses.definition: a single act of trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 一次努力去做的行动
senses.example: Her first attempt failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一次尝试失败了。
senses.why: The same word works as a noun naming one round of effort, which is why attempts are counted and can be called first or failed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也作名词，指一轮努力，因此尝试可以计数，也能说第一次或失败的尝试。

intro.en: Attempt is a Latin word of testing, and a try is a reach made to see what happens.
intro.cn: attempt 是拉丁语中表示试探的词，一次尝试就是一次试探性的伸手。

items.en: temptare meant 'to try or test'.
items.cn: temptare 意为「尝试、试探」。

items.en: attemptare meant 'to try to reach'.
items.cn: attemptare 意为「试着够到」。

items.en: atempter meant 'to attempt or risk'.
items.cn: atempter 意为「尝试、冒险」。

items.en: English attempt covered both the effort and the risk.
items.cn: 英语 attempt 兼指努力与冒险。

items.en: The noun use settled for one round of effort.
items.cn: 名词用法固定为一轮努力。

note.en: The look-alike group is the tempt family; the near-meaning group gives other words for trying.
note.cn: 形近组是 tempt 词族；近义组是其他表示尝试的词。

normalIntro.en: An attempt is a reach whose result is still unknown.
normalIntro.cn: attempt 是一次结果尚未可知的伸手。

normal.en: The verb pattern is attempt to do, not attempt doing.
normal.cn: 动词结构是 attempt to do。

normal.en: As a noun it is countable: an attempt, three attempts.
normal.cn: 作名词可数：一次尝试、三次尝试。

normal.en: In an attempt to introduces a purpose.
normal.cn: in an attempt to 引出目的。

normal.en: Attempt is more formal than try.
normal.cn: attempt 比 try 正式。

normal.en: The final pt is pronounced as a clear t.
normal.cn: 词尾的 pt 读作清晰的 t。

abstract.en: See fingers an inch short of the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离把手还差一点。

abstract.en: See a door pushed once and then again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被推了一次又一次。

abstract.en: See a mark on a wall counting failed tries.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上记着一次次失败的刻痕。

examples.en: He attempted to open the stuck door.
examples.cn: 他试图推开那扇卡住的门。

examples.en: Her first attempt failed.
examples.cn: 她的第一次尝试失败了。

examples.en: They made no attempt to hide the mistake.
examples.cn: 他们没有试图掩盖这个错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tempt（试探）：向目标伸手试一试，就是试图；试的这一轮，就是一次尝试。

root: 源自拉丁语 attemptare「试着够到」，由 ad-「向」与 temptare「尝试、试探」构成，经古法语 atempter 进入英语；动词指努力去做，名词指一轮尝试。

sensesIntro.en: The act of trying and one round of it share a single word.
sensesIntro.cn: 试着去做的动作与其中的一轮，共用同一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stretched out and not yet arriving.
core.cn: 核心意象：手伸出去，还没够到。

intro.en: The tempt root, 'to try', also gives temptation and tempt.
intro.cn: 词根 tempt 意为「试探」，也构成 temptation 与 tempt。

latinIntro.en: Latin temptare meant to test, and testing someone's will became tempting them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temptare 意为试探，试探一个人的意志就变成了引诱。
